To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adamantyl group is important for antiviral activities, and that the antiviral activities are dependent on the stereochemistry and the number of adamantyl groups.
the antiviral activity of N-carbamoylated and N-acylated derivatives of symmetrical amines was investigated, and that a few derivatives with adamantyl groups showed significant activity.
N-carbamoylated or N-acylated derivatives of symmetrical amines, especially 1,2- diamino- and 1,2-bis(phenylethyl)amino- compounds, showed antiviral activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of N-carbamoyldiamine and N-acyldiamine derivatives, and the evaluation of their antiviral activity.
the synthesis and antiviral activity of N-mono and N,N'-di-substituted derivatives of (1R, 2R)-1 and meso-1 as well as (1R, R)-3 and meso-3.
the synthesis of N-carbamoylamino and/or N-acylamino derivatives of symmetrical amines and evaluation of their antiviral activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adamantyl group(s), especially in the cis configuration of 1, 2, 2'-triaminocyclohaxane, was found to be a useful group for antiviral agents, and the 1, 3, 3'-trisubstituted derivative of meso-1 and meso-3 showed a better antiviral effect than that of the corresponding 1, 1', 3-trisubstituted derivatives.
the N-carbamoylated or N,N'-carbamoylated diamines, especially the N-acylated derivatives of (1R, 2R)-1 and/or (1R,3R)-3, were more active against HSV-1.

the N-carbamoylation and/or N,N'-(di)acylation of symmetrical diamine derivatives with an appropriate spacer length, such as 1,2-cyclohexane or 1,2-phenylethane, could be a promising approach to design new antiviral agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antiviral activity of N-carbamoylated and/or N-acylated diamine derivatives depends on the type of diamine, the length and the nature of the spacer between the two amine groups and/or the nature of the carbamoyl and acetyl groups.
N-acyl and/or N-carbamoylated diamines were synthesized and their antiviral activities against HSV-1 were evaluated.
a few compounds with adamantyl group showed significant antivirality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adamantane moiety is a key structural feature for the anti-HSV-1 activity.
the antiviral activities against HSV-1 of these compounds are not dependent on their lipophilicity.
the introduction of adamantyl group(s), especially cis-configuration, to the N-terminus of 1, 2-diaminocylohexane derivatives is important for antiviral activities against HSV-1.
